newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell off troubled hydro-electric plant.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell off troubled hydro-electric plant.

text.p: The government will sell off a 340 megawatt hydro-electric power plant in northwest Colombia when it comes on stream in 1999, the generator's acting chairman said Thursday.
The construction of the Urra plant, located on the Sinu River in Cordoba province, began in 1992 and has been plagued by logistical, geological and financial problems from the outset.
The initial projected cost of $690 million has since increased to more than $715 million.

The government is virtually the sole owner of the plant, except for a tiny shareholding by a local businessmen's group, and has been forced to approve an additional $197 million credit line to bail out the troubled construction process.

"Initial costs rose as we realized more civil engineering works were necessary than first thought. The geological conditions were also much tougher," said Felix Barreneche, acting chairman of the Urra project.
He denied the government would be selling the plant to rid itself of a financial drain, saying that the sell-off was part of the Samper administration's overall privatization policy.
"There are good prospects for private investors in this plant depending of course what price the government is looking for," Barreneche said.
The construction of the plant and dam, which has involved diverting the course of the Sinu River, has meant displacing 650 families of peasant-farmers.
The government was due to announce the winning bids in the sell-off of two hydro-electric plants and five coal and gas-fired power plants Thursday and Friday.
